The must-sees

8 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Neighbourhood

    Albaicín

    It was a densely populated town in Nasrid times and kept its street plan after 1492. Many houses are carmenes, homes with walled gardens.

    Look for

    Watch for aljibes at street corners: old Moorish cisterns with arched openings that stored water for the quarter.

  2. 02
    Palace

    Alhambra Nasrid Palaces

    They were built mostly in the 14th century under Yusuf I and Muhammad V. The Court of the Lions, with its fountain of twelve stone lions, is the best known of the courtyards.

    Look for

    On the walls, find the Nasrid motto carved again and again in Arabic: wa la ghaliba illa Allah, there is no victor but God.

  3. 03
    Landmark

    Carrera del Darro

    It is one of the oldest streets in the city. Old houses, churches and the remains of a Moorish bridge line the way.

    Look for

    Step into El Bañuelo, an 11th-century Arab bathhouse whose vaults are pierced with star-shaped skylights.

  4. 04
    Palace

    Generalife

    It was a country retreat close to the palace, with orchards fed by the royal water channel. Its Court of the Water Channel is lined with fountains along a long pool.

    Look for

    On the Water Stairway, water runs down channels cut into the tops of the handrails.

  5. 05
    Church

    Granada Cathedral

    Work began in 1523 and Diego de Siloé turned the Gothic plan toward the Renaissance. The painter and sculptor Alonso Cano designed the main facade in the 17th century.

    Look for

    Cano designed the facade like a giant triumphal arch, with three tall, deeply recessed arches.

  6. 06
    Viewpoint

    Mirador de San Nicolás

    At sunset the walls of the Alhambra turn red, the colour that gave it its name, the red one. Buskers and flamenco guitarists often play here.

    Look for

    Pick out the Comares Tower, the tallest of the Alhambra’s towers: it holds the sultans’ throne room, the Hall of the Ambassadors.

  7. 07
    Church · 1517

    Royal Chapel

    Isabella and Ferdinand chose to be buried in the city they conquered in 1492. Their marble tombs lie next to those of their daughter Juana and her husband Philip.

    Look for

    A gilded wrought-iron screen by Maestro Bartolomé of Jaén closes off the royal tombs.

  8. 08
    Neighbourhood

    Sacromonte

    Gitano families made their homes in these caves for centuries. Its cave venues are known for zambra, a local style of flamenco.

    Look for

    Watch for whitewashed chimneys poking out of the hillside: often the only part of a cave home you can see.
